articles.title: SJAA EPHEMERIS
articles.summary: The SJAA EPHEMERIS details upcoming events for the San Jose Astronomical Association from late March through May, including numerous star parties at Houge Park, dedicated Dark Sky weekends at Henry Coe Park, astronomy classes, and their annual auction. Additionally, the article announces the annual SJAA Yosemite Public Star Party in July, offering free admission and camping to volunteers at Glacier Point in exchange for public outreach.

articles.title: APRIL 2009
articles.summary: This document is a calendar for April 2009, featuring daily highlights that combine celestial events, historical dates in space exploration, and various awareness days with educational content. Each entry provides links and references to activities, articles, and games from NASA's 'The Space Place' website, focusing on space science, mathematics, and Earth-related topics for educational purposes.

articles.title: Pluto visits the states
articles.summary: This article presents an astronomical ephemeris for April 2009, detailing observable planets like Saturn, Mercury, Venus (including an occultation by the Moon), and Mars (conjunctions with Venus and Uranus). It also humorously discusses recent resolutions from New Mexico and Illinois declaring Pluto a planet within their state boundaries, sparking commentary on Pluto's controversial status and the practical implications of such declarations.

articles.title: Where did all these gadgets come from?!
articles.summary: NASA's New Millennium Program (NMP) is crucial for flight-testing innovative space technologies, such as ion propulsion and AI, before they are integrated into real missions. By validating these advanced systems, NMP significantly reduces risk and enables ambitious space exploration projects like the Dawn mission, which relies on ion propulsion, and has enhanced numerous other probes, including the Mars rovers and the New Horizons mission. The program's success demonstrates that in-space validation is key to widespread technology adoption across deep-space missions.

articles.title: Mailing List Policy
articles.summary: This document outlines the San Jose Astronomical Association's (SJAA) mailing list policy, detailing open posting with moderation for non-board members and highlighting increased transparency through public links and visible subscriber lists. Separately, it includes an astronomical analysis of Pluto's declination, concluding that it will never be observed directly overhead from locations like New Mexico or Illinois due to its maximum northern declination, thus challenging its planetary status based on this criterion.

articles.title: The Last Month In Astronomy
articles.summary: This astronomy report for February-March 2009 details several significant events, including the successful launch of the Kepler spacecraft to search for exoplanets and the discovery of a binary black hole. It also covers the deliberate lunar crash of China's Chang'e 1, the launch failure of the Orbiting Carbon Observatory, and the upcoming Planck mission to study the Cosmic Microwave Background. Additionally, the article notes a local talk by Christopher McKay discussing Mars findings.

articles.title: Loaners
articles.summary: The article describes a club's loaner program, which allows members to try various telescopes of different sizes and technologies before making a purchase. Highlighted as a significant member benefit, the program caters to all experience levels and maintains a constantly changing inventory of available scopes.

articles.title: Deep Sky Objects
articles.summary: The article presents three recommended deep sky objects for observation in March, categorized by difficulty: NGC 2567 (easy open cluster), NGC 2613 (medium edge-on spiral galaxy), and Abell 29 (difficult planetary nebula). For each object, it provides celestial coordinates, a brief description, and apparent magnitude. The article also includes a trivia question about a distant bright star, Deneb.
